title: Integrable Chiral Quantum Field Theories with Spacetime-Dependent Interactions
abstract: We construct a class of integrable chiral fermionic quantum field theories with interactions depending on both space and time. The construction starts with a unitary, regular, difference-form two-body scattering matrix that satisfies braiding unitarity and the Yang--Baxter equation. Each freely moving right- or left-moving particle carries a characteristic coordinate that remains constant along its trajectory, and the scattering matrix depends on differences of these coordinates. The many-body amplitudes form a discrete connection over coordinate-ordering sectors. The Yang--Baxter equation gives its local flatness, while periodicity on a spatial circle produces quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov difference equations expressing global flatness. In terms of a reference amplitude satisfying the exchange and qKZ constraints, these transports determine the exact fixed-particle-number wavefunction. We derive the characteristic form of the spacetime-dependent interaction and illustrate the construction with a chiral $SU(2)$ Gross--Neveu realization. Independent reparametrizations of the right- and left-moving characteristics yield genuine space-time dependence, whereas equal-slope affine maps recover the spatially homogeneous, time-dependent case.
summary: This work develops a systematic method to construct integrable chiral quantum field theories with interactions that vary both in space and time. By enforcing consistency conditions derived from the Yang-Baxter and qKZ equations, the authors determine the exact form of the spacetime-dependent coupling. This provides a powerful theoretical framework for studying non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated fermionic systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the construction of integrable chiral fermionic quantum field theories whose interactions explicitly depend on both space and time.
main_result: The authors derive the characteristic form of the spacetime-dependent interaction, successfully generalizing previous constructions to include genuine space-time dependence via nonaffine reparametrizations.
method: The construction relies on satisfying the Yang–Baxter equation (for local flatness) and the quantum Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (qKZ) difference equations (for global flatness on a spatial circle).
model_or_system: The system is a chiral fermionic quantum field theory, exemplified by a chiral SU(2) Gross-Neveu realization, governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian H_ch(t).
key_observables: The coupling function g(x, t) and the resulting exact fixed-particle-number wavefunction.
important_parameters: The parameters defining the scattering matrix and the spatial/temporal modulation scales (e.g., $\kappa,  eta, A, B, \ell$).
main_assumptions: The existence of a unitary, regular, difference-form two-body scattering matrix satisfying specific algebraic relations, and the compatibility of conserved quantities with time-ordered evolution.
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory by starting with the scattering matrix, establishing local flatness via the Yang-Baxter equation, and then imposing global flatness via the qKZ equations. The final steps derive the explicit form of the spacetime-dependent interaction and apply it to the SU(2) Gross-Neveu model.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting integrability (YBE/qKZ) to explicit time- and space-dependent couplings provides powerful tools for modeling non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated quantum systems.
